cases.title: UX audit with vague flow context
cases.prompt: Audit this onboarding flow for friction. I do not have screenshots handy. The product is a B2B analytics dashboard and the flow is signup -> connect data source -> first dashboard.

behaviors: Clearly labels the audit as low confidence because no screenshots were provided.
Still provides useful likely friction points and validation steps.
Asks no more than three clarifying questions.
Invents visible UI details.
Refuses to proceed because screenshots are missing.

cases.title: Accessibility review without focus states
cases.prompt: Do an accessibility review for a checkout form. Context: fields for email, shipping address, payment, a disabled Pay button until required fields are valid, and inline errors after submit. I only have this text description.

behaviors: Frames issues as risks to verify, not confirmed WCAG failures.
Covers keyboard, labels/names, color/contrast, motion, and states.
Includes concrete checks for disabled and error states.
Claims compliance without inspecting implementation.
Relies on color alone for error communication.

cases.title: Analytics hypotheses from partial funnel data
cases.prompt: Given this funnel, tell me what UX changes to try. Time window: last 14 days. Segment: trial users on web. Steps: viewed_import_page 10,000; clicked_connect_source 4,200; auth_success 2,900; first_import_complete 1,300. No event definitions are documented.

behaviors: Identifies the largest visible drop-off from provided counts.
Does not invent event semantics beyond the names supplied.
Ranks hypotheses with mechanism, expected signal, fastest test, and risk.
Invents benchmarks or significance.
Treats event names as fully defined behavior.

cases.title: Component spec with token-first constraints
cases.prompt: Write a component spec for a Status Badge used in tables and cards. It needs success, warning, danger, neutral, and info variants, plus loading and disabled states. Keep it engineering-ready.

behaviors: Prefers existing variants and semantic token hooks before one-off styles.
Defines content length and truncation/wrapping guidance.
Calls out invalid combinations.
Uses hardcoded color values as the primary spec.
Omits loading or disabled behavior.

cases.title: Feature spec with unresolved decisions
cases.prompt: Write a design spec for saved dashboard filters. Users can save, rename, duplicate, share, and delete filters. Some filters are private, some are shared with a team. We have not decided permissions yet.

behaviors: Does not finalize permission rules that are explicitly undecided.
Identifies edge cases around sharing, deletion, and rename conflicts.
Includes a verification plan.
Invents a permission model as fact.
Skips open questions.

cases.title: Research synthesis from thin notes
cases.prompt: Synthesize these notes from 3 users evaluating a data import flow: P1: 'I am not sure what permissions this needs.' P2: 'The CSV errors are hard to fix.' P3: 'I expected a sample dashboard after import.' Turn this into themes, insights, opportunities, and follow-up questions.

behaviors: Uses the snippets as evidence without overstating sample size.
Keeps confidence appropriately low or medium.
Turns insights into falsifiable hypotheses or success signals.
Overgeneralizes from three snippets.
Invents participant demographics or intent.

cases.title: State plan with offline and failure modes
cases.prompt: Create an empty/loading/error/success state plan for a Notifications center in a SaaS app. It must cover first-time empty, all caught up, offline, server error, and permissions blocked.

behaviors: Distinguishes true empty from success empty.
Defines recovery actions for offline, server error, and permissions blocked.
Communicates state with more than color.
Treats every empty state as the same message.
Omits recovery actions.

cases.title: Competitive audit without named competitors
cases.prompt: Run a competitive design audit for bulk user invite flows in B2B admin tools. I do not have competitor names. The decision is whether we should support CSV upload in v1.

behaviors: States assumptions about comparator selection.
Gives one recommended approach with an escape hatch.
Frames what evidence to capture next.
Claims to have inspected competitors without provided evidence.
Provides a long menu without a recommendation.

cases.title: Figma triage with likely bad node target
cases.prompt: Update this Figma screen to match our new empty state pattern: https://www.figma.com/file/example?node-id=maybe-bad. Make the changes directly.

behaviors: Triages the request before attempting writes.
Requests or verifies a valid target node and desired scope.
States safe stop conditions for write actions.
Claims a Figma write without tool evidence.
Proceeds as if the node is valid without verification.

cases.title: Synthesize conflicting agent recommendations
cases.prompt: Three agents reviewed the same dashboard setup flow. UX audit says reduce steps from 5 to 3. Accessibility review says the current single-page form is already too dense and needs better grouping. Analytics says the biggest drop is at data-source auth. Synthesize a recommendation and call out conflicts.

behaviors: Does not average the recommendations into a vague compromise.
Prioritizes the highest-confidence behavioral bottleneck.
Names the conflict between fewer steps and cognitive/accessibility density.
Ignores one of the three agents.
Recommends a redesign without validation signals.

cases.title: Design review synthesis with conflicting signals
cases.prompt: Synthesize these inputs into one recommendation for a dashboard setup flow. UX audit: reduce setup from 5 steps to 3 because users feel the flow is long. Accessibility review: do not collapse everything into one page because grouping and focus order are already weak. Analytics: the biggest leak is data-source auth. Research: two users were unsure what permissions they were granting. We need a recommendation for the next sprint.

behaviors: Gives one recommended path instead of averaging all inputs.
Prioritizes the strongest behavioral bottleneck while preserving accessibility constraints.
Names what evidence is missing and what would change the recommendation.
Ignores either the accessibility conflict or analytics bottleneck.
Claims the research sample proves broad user behavior.
